text.p: - Nine people died in traffic accidents on Slovenian roads over the weekend, the police said.
- From January 1, Slovenians will no longer have to pay customs duty of about 40 percent on products imported from the European Union.

- Leader of conservative People's Party, Marjan Podobnik, said the alliance of three "Spring" parties is obligatory for his party, but they are looking for the fourth party as an equal partner to the alliance. "Spring" parties won 45 out of 90 parliamentary seats on the November 10 general election.

- United List of Social Democrats, which got nine seats at the general election, said they would support Janez Drnovsek as candidate for prime minister. President Milan Kucan is expected to name his candidate by the end of the year.
- Pivovarna Lasko beat Spanish Caja Cantabria by 24-20 in Saturday's fourth round match of Handball European Champions' League.
- Marjan Podobnik said he would start a court case against untruthful rumours in Slovenian media that he was treated in a psychiatrical hospital.
- Slovenia's Adria Airways said it would soon replace its aircrafts with smaller ones more appropriate for Adria's market. The new aircraft would come from Boeing and Canadair.
